Vanessa — thanks for this. A few clarifying questions before we escalate to procurement:

1) Term: Our leadership prefers 24 months for predictability, but we want a clear ramp window (we plan to go live regionally: US east -> EU within 6 months).
2) Pool sizing: The spreadsheet lists A100 and H100 SKUs. For our peak (3k concurrent sessions, median seq len 512) which pool do you recommend? Is there an option to start on A100 and switch to H100 mid-term?
3) Throughput guarantees: We need a defined per-minute throughput SLO and a ramp cadence with penalties / service credits if you miss guaranteed TPS.
4) Start date: We want the capacity available in the week of May 10 if possible.
5) Procurement: We favor quarterly invoicing if possible; will review if you require annual upfront.

Can you and your team outline a 24-month proposal with an accelerated ramp option and an initial 4-week pilot (reduced commit) so legal/procurement have something concrete?

Best,
Emily Zhang
Head of Product, Skyware.ai

Emily / team — attached is a focused quote (see summary below). I kept the math simple and included three invoice options. I also added an accelerated-ramp credit we can apply if you hit the faster onboarding milestones.

Summary (24-month focused):
- Commit: 200K GPU-hours/month equivalent (A100 baseline)
- Unit price (A100-equivalent): $0.018 / GPU-hour (net, 24mo tier).
- Discount lift for 36mo: additional 12% off net unit price.
- Accelerated ramp (target full throughput in 6 weeks): $25k one-time enablement credit applied if Skyware reaches production traffic within 6 weeks.
- Pilot: 4-week pilot at 25% of committed units (billed at pilot rate), pilot fees credited to committed spend if converted within 30 days.

Invoice cadence options:
A) Quarterly invoicing (net 30) — default we recommend for book-keeping.
B) Monthly invoicing (net 30) — small processing uplift of 2% on net.
C) Annual prepay — 5% additional discount on total.

Start-date & capacity: earliest guaranteed reservation week is May 10-16, pending signed order and initial deposit (we typically require a 30% initial deposit for reserved pools to lock GPUs). If you need an earlier slot we can discuss short-term burst capacity but that’s subject to availability and a premium.

Attached: redwood_skyware_reserved_commit_options_20270420.pdf (updated pricing sheet) and capacity_ramp_matrix.xlsx (detailed month-by-month).

Happy to hop on a 30-min sync with procurement to walk terms.

— Marcus

Emily — quick technical notes on capacity and SLOs to complement Marcus’s commercial note: 

1) Pool recommendation: For 3k concurrent, seq len 512, we recommend starting on an A100 pool sized to 220K GPU-hours/month equivalent for predictable latency at your target tail. A switch to H100 later is supported via a model-variant rollout; we’ll validate perf in a staging slot before migration.

2) Throughput SLOs: We can commit to a per-minute token throughput SLO with a monthly uptime SLA. Example: 99.5% of minutes >= target TPS across the month. If SLA missed, service credits scale: 5% credit for single missband, up to 20% for sustained miss over rolling 7-day window. I’ll paste suggested SLA wording into the contract draft.

3) Ramp schedule (accelerated):
- Week 1–2: pilot + validation (~25% commit)
- Week 3–6: incremental ramp to 100% (rollout US prod by Week 6)
- Month 3–6: EU onboarding and cross-region replication
4) Earliest start: If you sign and provide deposit by EOD Apr 30 we can target reservation + engineering onboarding the week of May 10. Otherwise next guaranteed window is May 24.

5) Monitoring and rollback: we’ll provide per-route token cost and tail-latency dashboards, plus automatic fallback to a compatible smaller model variant in the event of sustained capacity pressure.

If Procurement wants specific SLA language, point me at the clause and I’ll draft exact text.

— Dev
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
